transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-20
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (CTO, Acropolis), Tom Reilly (Platform Engineer), Sara Chen (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Quick product walkthrough of rate limiting and multi-tenant controls. Demoed console patterns and API examples. Customer interested in predictable burst handling and per-tenant cost controls; security wants SSO+audit log detail.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Jordan from Redwood. Quick roundtable?
[00:06] Maya: Maya here, CTO at Acropolis. Tom and Sara with me.
[00:10] Tom: Tom, platform.
[00:12] Sara: Sara, security ops.
[00:14] Jordan: Great. Priya, SE, will run the demo. Rough agenda: show org/project key patterns, quota flavors, burst gating and sticky routing.
[00:22] Priya: Thanks — hi all. I'll share my screen in a sec. We have a short deck plus live Console and API examples — link: https://redwood.app/decks/tenant-patterns (note: link auto-truncated).
[00:35] [screen share starts]
[00:37] Priya: Alright, first principle — we recommend two logical layers of keys: org-level keys for global quotas and observability, and project keys for app-level enforcement and billing.
[00:50] Tom: Can you show an example where a single customer has multiple projects? We want per-team fairshare but also org wide commitments.
[01:02] Priya: Yeah — show console: Organization -> Projects -> Keys. Here we have Acropolis-Org with three projects: integrations, analytics, chat-service. Each project has a project-key. Org-key sits above and can apply hard limits or soft fairshare.
[01:18] Priya: The key distinction: org-key can act as a parent quota that prevents noisy-projects from taking all capacity; project-keys let teams have independent billing and per-route rate limits.
[01:30] Maya: Do org keys impact billing? We bill per-project today so we need to preserve that.
[01:36] Jordan: Good question. Billing is orthogonal — you can route billing back to projects while enforcing org-level rate fences. So cost attribution stays per project.
[01:45] Priya: Now rate-limiting modes: strict per-key quota (hard cap), fairshare smoothing (proportional allocation based on configured weights), and burst windows (allow short bursts above baseline then smooth down).
[01:58] Tom: That burst window — is it token bucket style?
[02:01] Priya: It's similar; we call it 'burst buffer' in the console. Under the hood it's a sliding window that allows X extra tokens for Y seconds, then enforcement. It's configurable per org or per project.
[02:14] Tom: Could be useful for our nightly batch jobs that spike briefly. Can we whitelist certain routes?
[02:19] Priya: Yes — route-level overrides exist. You can mark some endpoints as exempt up to a cap, and you can attach per-route quotas (e.g., embedding endpoints vs chat generation).
[02:30] Sara: Security question — where are logs kept and how long? We need audit trails for admin actions and per-token usage.
[02:39] Jordan: By default we retain operational logs for 90 days; enterprise customers can extend retention, ship logs to their SIEM, or enable retention to customer-managed S3. We also have detailed per-request traces available in Console for 30 days.
[02:54] Sara: Is that compatible with our KMS/HSM?
[02:57] Priya: Yes — for Private deployments we support customer KMS integrations and HSM. For hosted, we have KMS-backed keys and we can discuss bring-your-own-key options.
[03:07] Maya: On the routing side — we have regional constraints. If we want US traffic pinned, can routing respect region and also prefer cheaper model variants during peak?
[03:18] Priya: Absolutely — Smart routing policies let you specify region preference, cost tiers, and fallbacks. So during capacity pressure you can route to a quantized variant or lower-cost model for non-critical routes.
[03:30] Tom: How does sticky routing work? We have session affinity concerns — we don't want a user mid-chat to switch model variants unexpectedly.
[03:38] Priya: The sticky routing feature keys on session-id or project-key and keeps the same model variant for the duration of a session (configurable TTL). We also do KV cache affinity for low-latency continuation — note: sometimes the transcriptions say 'K V cache' for KV cache.
[03:53] Jordan: Quick demo: I'll show the API payload for org vs project key. Here is an org-key header and a project-key header. If both are provided, enforcement favors the stricter rule but metrics attribute to the project.
[04:10] [console typing noises]
[04:15] Priya: Example policy: org-rate: 1M tokens/day, project-rate: 100k tokens/day, project-weight: 2x for analytics during business hours.
[04:30] Tom: If analytics needs bursts at midnight for backfills, can we schedule temporary bump?
[04:36] Priya: Yes — via Console you can create scheduled overrides or use the API to create ephemeral policy windows. We also support programmatic escalation from an orchestrator.
[04:48] Maya: Are there hard SLOs for latency if we enforce strict fairshare? We worry about increased tail latency.
[04:56] Priya: The runtime is designed to maintain latency SLOs; when we throttle, we have two behaviors: queue-and-serve (small delay) or immediate 429. You configure for low-latency vs strict fairness. For very latency-sensitive endpoints we recommend reserving a dedicated slice or using Dedicated capacity.
[05:15] Tom: How do we test this? Can we emulate our 2k RPS burst?
[05:20] Priya: We'll run a short Dedicated trial with a synthetic workload. I can provision a 4-GPU pool for a week and run your replay. We'll capture latency percentiles and cost.
[05:30] Jordan: Action item: Priya will run the replay; Tom will send the traffic dump.
[05:34] [10-minute demo jump — console walkthrough continues, timestamps jump forward]
[15:40] Priya: Next section is quotas UI — here you can see a graph of spend vs quota, breakouts by route, and per-key usage. You can set alerts at X% of quota and automations to throttle or reroute traffic.
[15:55] Tom: Is there a hard policy language or JSON spec for these rules?
[16:00] Priya: Yes — policy-as-config. We show a JSON example: {"scope":"org","rules":[{"route":"/v1/chat","quota_per_min":200}]} — minor transcription artifacts in the log sometimes escape braces. We'll share the spec doc.
[16:15] Maya: We're also concerned about project onboarding — devs spinning up keys. Can we have provisioning flows with approvals?
[16:23] Priya: Console supports request-to-create workflows and role-based approval gates. You can require a manager approval before project-key is active.
[16:33] Sara: And SSO? We must integrate Okta and SCIM provisioning.
[16:37] Jordan: We support SAML/SSO and SCIM; we'll share an integration guide. Enterprise packages include SSO config assistance.
[16:48] Priya: A quick aside on cost controls: Optimize suggests batching, quantization, and per-route model recommendations. For multi-tenant loads, enabling prefix caching and KV affinity can lower token costs by up to 30% in real workloads.
[17:05] Tom: Prefix caching — does that leak context between tenants?
[17:09] Priya: No. Caches are keyed per-tenant and per-session unless you explicitly enable shared caching (not recommended for regulated data).
[17:18] [minor crosstalk]
[17:20] Maya: For compliance, we need to ensure personal data isn't retained beyond X days and we must be able to delete customer data on demand.
[17:28] Priya: We have data deletion APIs and retention policies. For Private deployments you can enforce air-gapped storage. We'll put the documentation link in the follow-up.
[17:38] Jordan: Let's walk through a hypothetical: Acropolis wants a 500k tokens/day org cap, per project 100k but analytics gets 2x weight from 9-17. If chat gets heavy, we want chat to throttle gracefully and route less-important tasks to a quantized model.
[17:58] Priya: I created a sample policy in the Console to illustrate; here's the timeline view and the smoothing curve for burst windows. You can edit weights and preview the effect on simulated traffic.
[18:12] Tom: Preview simulation — can it import our actual traffic distribution?
[18:17] Priya: We can accept CSV traffic dumps and replay them in the simulator; that gives you accurate projected token burn and collision points.
[18:26] Maya: About sticky routing TTL — what if a host failure forces a session to a different GPU with different cache; how do you handle KV cache warm-up?
[18:36] Priya: We do cache affinity best-effort; if fallback occurs we have fast warm-up paths and optional prefetching. There's a trade-off with cost; we can discuss dedicated warm pools for critical services.
[18:50] Sara: Are audit logs write-once? Tamper-evidence?
[18:54] Jordan: Logs can be shipped to your immutable ledger or SIEM. For Private customers we can set append-only S3 buckets and HSM-backed signing.
[19:05] [pause]
[19:10] Priya: Now a quick look at API examples — using org-key in header: 
Authorization: Bearer org_key_XXXX
X-Project-Key: project_key_YYYY
If project key is present, cost attribution goes to project_key_YYYY but enforcement is intersection of both policies.
[19:34] Tom: If enforcement intersects, which wins? Intersection meaning the lowest allowance?
[19:39] Priya: Correct — we enforce the stricter limit to protect the org. But you can set orphan allowances to let projects exceed temporarily and reconcile billing later.
[19:50] Maya: Can we set different penalties? For example, priority customers get queueing instead of 429s.
[19:58] Priya: We have policy actions: queue, 429, reroute to fallback model, or notify and auto-scale (if on Dedicated). Priority tiers can be applied to keys.
[20:11] Jordan: Quick security note — we redact PII in logs by default and provide field-level scrubbing rules you can tune.
[20:20] Sara: Good. Also we need to see pen-test results and recent SOC2 report.
[20:25] Jordan: We'll attach SOC2 report and a short pen test summary in the follow-up.
[20:30] [demo wraps up — questions and next steps]
[20:33] Maya: This looks promising. Two big asks: 1) run our replay, 2) enable a short Dedicated evaluation with burst profile.
[20:41] Jordan: Agreed. Priya, you got the replay?
[20:45] Priya: Yes — Tom said he'd upload to the shared drive — link: drive.company/acropolis/replay (placeholder). We'll schedule the Dedicated spin-up.
[20:54] Tom: Timeline — if we get the replay by Monday, can we start trials the same week?
[20:58] Priya: We can usually provision within 48 hours for a trial pool.
[21:02] Jordan: I'll follow up with pricing estimates for Dedicated trial and sample SOW.
[21:08] Sara: For procurement — what's the minimum commitment?
[21:12] Jordan: For short trials: no long-term commitment. For reserved Dedicated, we discuss monthly/annual commits. We'll outline options in the follow-up email.
[21:22] Maya: Any blockers on our side? Only need to confirm legal and security intake — Sara will coordinate.
[21:28] Sara: I'll send required compliance checklist and also request network diagrams.
[21:33] Jordan: Great. Final recap: Jordan sends playbook + SOC2 + pricing; Priya runs replay and trial; Tom supplies traffic dump; Sara shares compliance list.
[21:46] Maya: Thanks. One small nit — can we get a short written pattern for org/project keys and an example in Terraform?
[21:53] Priya: Yes — we'll include a Terraform snippet and Console screenshots.
[21:58] Jordan: Any other questions?
[22:00] [some small chat and wrap-up]
[22:10] Meeting end.
